audit_notes: Permeability check: straight channels d = 40 um at porosity 0.5: Kx = phi r^2/8 = 0.5*(20e-6)^2/8 = 2.5e-11 m2, consistent with 3e-11. sqrt(Kx) = 5.5 um -> sqrt(Kx+) = 1.0; sqrt(Kz) = 1.0 um -> sqrt(Kz+) = 0.19. Gomez-de-Segura & Garcia-Mayoral (JFM 2019): in the linear regime Delta U+ ~ sqrt(Kx+) - sqrt(Kz+) (virtual-origin difference, Brinkman slip lengths), valid while the wall-normal permeability stays small, sqrt(Ky+) < ~0.4 (otherwise spanwise Kelvin-Helmholtz rollers appear and drag increases). This requires the face perforations to limit Ky to < (0.4*5.4e-6)^2 = 4.7e-12 m2 - a hard design constraint not in the parameters. Slip used: 5.5 - 1.0 = 4.5 um -> expected gain 4.5/99.5 = 4.5% (theoretical maximum in the linear regime; roughness of the perforated face not included). Channel Reynolds number U_c d/nu with U_c ~ u at y+~1 = 0.22 m/s -> 7.4 (Stokes/ Darcy flow valid). Structural: 150 um silicone skin with 50% porosity has ~1/4 of the bulk stiffness; under 50 Pa shear and 1 bar static pressure (the channels are pressure-equalised) no collapse. Durability: 40 um channels and perforations are exactly the size of diatoms and bacterial colonies; clogging within weeks to months is the dominant risk. Baseline: impermeable smooth FR wall (both permeabilities 0).

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs clean FR hull
